title: Grouped NVFP4 route and quantized compute

sources.notes: Primary eight-stage behavior: route histogram/scan/scatter/gather, backend-selected gate-up, finite overflow scaling, down GEMM, atomic or fixed-order output; device arithmetic and scheduling are explicit abstractions.
Public raw-pointer tensor and scratch shape contract; false return delegates fallback to the caller and no exception crosses the boundary.
Models process-lifetime queue/primitive/scale caches, geometry stability, canonical scale copy and permanent atomic disarm after any caught internal failure.
oneDNN grouped-leg contract: allocation capacity versus device offsets, bank-native packed weights, asynchronous in-order submission, and false-without-serving refusal.
Imported Xe2 GEMM mainloop with local NVFP4 dtype/E4M3 group-scale decode and bank-native scale indexing; exact DPAS, copy, rounding and subgroup behavior are not modeled.
Imported tile-policy catalog plus local group-16 K-tile and FP32-store policies. The model preserves selection branches, not tile geometry performance.
Imported grouped scheduling, packed expert offsets, group-size dispatch and persistent atomic work queue; modeled as each grouped GEMM leg and reused atom scratch.
Shell build recipe has no program symbols; builds the vendored MXFP4 speed harness with required SYCL/CUTLASS definitions and SPIR-V extensions, not a serving binary.
Shell build recipe has no program symbols; links the current grouped wrapper objects and oneDNN for A/B verification.
Shell build recipe has no program symbols; shadows vendor Xe2 headers with the local group-16/NVFP4 fork for policy probing.
Shell build recipe has no program symbols; compiles and links the oneDNN numerical/performance probe against the vendor build tree.
Current full-entry deterministic fixture, finite/nonzero output check, backend dump and tolerance/cosine A/B comparison. Its tolerance contradicts a strict bit-equivalence reading.
CPU oracle and oneDNN harness for nibble order, E4M3 arithmetic, canonical scale repacking, empty expert groups, offsets as an upper bound, untouched padded tail and performance.
Historical real-bank full-layer timing harness. It predates current FP32 intermediate/output scratch, overflow-safe scaling and deterministic reduce; it is not current serving correctness behavior.
Speed-only policy sweep over vendored MXFP4 and optional forked NVFP4 policies; explicitly not a numerical correctness or production-path harness.
Controlled one-hot format harness for E4M3 scale decode, E2M1 nibble order, group-16 addressing and layout; not full MoE equivalence.
Data-only provenance marker with no code symbols: Xe2 machinery derives from vLLM-XPU kernel tree a07c4844; local changes add NVFP4 E4M3/group-16 to upstream MXFP4 E8M0/group-32.

assumptions: The caller supplies an in-order SYCL queue, live device-accessible pointers, and buffers with the shapes and capacities declared by grouped_moe.hpp.
Route IDs outside [0,E) are unowned compaction markers and are intentionally omitted rather than treated as errors.
The finite model's two experts, four routes and scalar arithmetic witness structure and algebra only; they do not stand for production sizing or floating-point bit equivalence.
Power-of-two scaling preserves the exact linear product algebraically, while FP16 narrowing, SiLU evaluation, DPAS order, non-finite inputs and float atomics require implementation checks.
The host rows-per-expert estimate divides by two because the source targets the shipped two-card split; it is not a topology-independent selection formula.
Environment-selected backend, big-tile arm and scatter mode are parsed once per process.
oneDNN queue/primitive and canonical scale caches, and successful MXFP4 derived-scale caches, intentionally live for the process/bank lifetime.
MXFP4 derived scales are approximate and quality-gated; they are never assumed equivalent to native NVFP4.
Copied Xe2/CUTE/CUTLASS-SYCL internals are external-derived machinery at tree a07c4844 with documented local NVFP4 changes, not a general first-party architecture claim.
Probe measurements and dated silicon comments are evidence from their captured configuration, not invariant performance guarantees.

implementation_checks.description: Use a small CPU route bucket/oracle to compare histogram totals, exclusive offsets, inverse-map membership and deterministic top-k weighted accumulation, including -1 and out-of-range route IDs.

Compare finite rows below, at and above FP16 overflow against a CPU calculation of the minimal power-of-two shift and restored weighted down-projection product; include Inf and NaN to inspect the finite-only branch.

Decode paired E4M3 scales on CPU, reproduce geometric-mean log2 rounding and compare every cached E8M0 byte; then quantify output error against the exact NVFP4 CPU oracle rather than requiring equality.
Source-inspect or CPU-drive an invalid live-cache geometry/failed allocation and confirm false return, one-time permanent g_armed clear, and native completion of the same leg.
Run the controlled 0x21/0x38 one-hot fixture when Xe2 hardware is available and require the low nibble to decode as even K with outputs alternating 0.5 and 1.0.
CPU-execute the scalar E2M1/E4M3 oracle for the small fixture and compare canonical-scale oneDNN output, empty-group handling, actual offsets and untouched padded tail.
Compare native and oneDNN full-entry dumps using the harness contract max_rel < 5e-2 and cosine > 0.9999; do not relabel this tolerance check as bit equivalence.
Source-inspect that NVFP4 remains in the four-bit offset family, group size 16 selects the group-16 instantiation, and the chosen native policies retain tile_k=16.
